goal: First concrete step of the config rule-INDUCER (operator direction): introspect the config games' INTERACTION model -- the foundation of the meta-learned library.
method: Per config game: click an object's cell repeatedly (does it cycle the cell's colour?) and try a keyboard action (does it change the grid?).
key_finding: Clicking a cell NEVER changes that cell's colour in ANY config game (the click_cell_seq is constant for all 9). So the interaction is INDIRECT: clicking a control toggles a target ELSEWHERE, or keyboard cycles a SELECTED element. This is exactly why Stage 2's executor failed -- it assumed DIRECT cell-recolor (click cell -> set its colour), which is the wrong model for every config game.

per_game.ka59: avail[1,2,3,4,6] nobj2 click_noeffect kbd_active -> keyboard-driven select/move
per_game.sc25: avail[1,2,3,4,6] nobj4 click_noeffect kbd_inert -> click toggles indirectly
per_game.tn36: avail[6] nobj21 click_noeffect kbd_inert -> click-only, indirect toggle
per_game.tr87: avail[1,2,3,4] nobj7 no_click kbd_active -> keyboard cycles selected element (glyph-rewrite)
per_game.s5i5: avail[6] nobj13 click_noeffect kbd_inert -> click-only, indirect toggle
per_game.g50t: avail[1,2,3,4,5] nobj5 no_click kbd_inert -> keyboard needs selection first

implication_for_rule_inducer: POSITIVE for the operator's direction: the config games share a SMALL, LEARNABLE interaction vocabulary (~2-3 types: keyboard-cycle/move-selected, click-toggle-indirect), NOT bespoke per-game mechanics. So a meta-learned library of interaction patterns IS viable -- introspection can classify a new game's interaction type from this vocabulary. The rule-inducer's introspection layer is feasible and is the first concrete piece. The next pieces: (1) MODEL each interaction type (what does keyboard-cycle do to the selected element? what does click toggle?), (2) induce the win-RULE on top (the relation the configuration must satisfy), (3) a search that uses the CORRECT interaction model (fixing the Stage 2 executor, which used direct-recolor).
